subject: Decomposing observed intercepts in MTMM model

messages.author: 469ab9abdba35033
messages.subject: Decomposing observed intercepts in MTMM model
parts:
Hi, everyone,
I was wondering how to impose constraints on observed variables’ intercepts to decompose them into method-specific and construct-specific components in an MTMM model.
Assume, I have 3 traits (A, B, and C) and 3 methods (X, Y, and Z), then the MTMM model looks somewhat like this:
#trait space
A =~ ovAX + ovAY + ovAZ
B =~ ovBX + ovBY + ovBZ
C =~ ovCX + ovCY + ovCZ
#method space
X =~ ovAX + ovBX + ovCX
Y =~ ovAY + ovBY + ovCY
Z =~ ovAZ + ovBZ + ovCZ
# orthogonality constraints between trait space and method space
…
But now, if I want to decompose intercepts of every observed variable into trait-specific and method-specific components, it should look somewhat like this:
#define intercepts’ labels
ovAX ~ iAX*1
ovAY ~ iAY*1
ovAZ ~ iAZ*1
ovBX ~ iBX*1
ovBY ~ iBY*1
ovBZ ~ iBZ*1
ovCX ~ iCX*1
ovCY ~ iCY*1
ovCZ ~ iCZ*1
#define trait-specific components
iA := iAX - (iAX + iAY + iAZ)/3
iB := iBX - (iBX + iBY + iBZ)/3
iC := iCX - (iCX + iCY + iCZ)/3
#define method-specific components
iX = iAX - iA
iY = iAY - iA
iZ = iAZ - iA
#constrain the remaining trait-method interactions
iBY == iB + iY
iCY == iC + iY

iBZ == iB + iZ
iCZ == iC + iZ
This approach works seemingly nice in lavaan, but fails to initiate sampling in blavaan with target=”stanclassic”.
How to estimate a model with such constraints in blavaan? Is my intuition about model-building wrong? Do I miss something? Should I provide some custom initiation values for the algorithm?

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Decomposing observed intercepts in MTMM model
parts:
Hi Denis,

blavaan is less sophisticated than lavaan when it comes to constraints. I am guessing that it has trouble with iA (and iB and iC) being defined via ":=" on one line, then iA (and iB and iC) also being used on the rhs of other equality constraints. You might see whether it helps to define iX, iY, iZ, iBY, iCY, etc without reference to iA, iB, and iC. For example, instead of

you might try

iX = (iAX + iAY + iAZ)/3
iY = iAY - (iAX - (iAX + iAY + iAZ)/3)
etc

And if you send the full model syntax, I can take a look in more detail (I believe your last email was just a snip of a larger model?).

Ed
